Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.persistence.adapter

Class UserRepositoryAdapter

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.persistence.adapter.UserRepositoryAdapter
All Implemented Interfaces:
UserRepository
@Component public class UserRepositoryAdapter extends Object implements UserRepository
Spring Data JPA-backed adapter for the UserRepository domain port.

Bridges the domain User aggregate to the UserJpa entity through UserMapper. The domain layer never sees JPA types; the application layer never sees Spring Data.

listAll(com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.domain.shared.Cursor, int) uses the same keyset paging strategy as ApiKeyRepositoryAdapter: fetch pageSize + 1 rows ordered (createdAt DESC, id DESC), trim the surplus, and emit a non-null nextCursor when more rows exist.

    • existsByEmail

      public boolean existsByEmail(Email email)
      Description copied from interface: UserRepository
      Returns true iff a user with the given email exists. Callers pass the canonicalized (lowercase) value via Email#value() — the lower(email) functional unique index (V004) keeps the lookup O(1). Used by CreateUserService (US-05-004) for the duplicate-email pre-flight check; the value-object encapsulation is what makes "supply the canonical value" a non-issue here.
      Specified by:
      existsByEmail in interface UserRepository

    • listAll

      public Page<User> listAll(Cursor cursor, int pageSize)
      Description copied from interface: UserRepository
      Returns one page of users ordered newest-first ((createdAt, id) DESC). Pass cursor = null for the first page. pageSize is the maximum number of items in the returned page; the adapter is responsible for detecting the presence of a next page and emitting a non-null Page.nextCursor() accordingly. Used by ListUsersService (US-05-005).
      Specified by:
      listAll in interface UserRepository

    • delete

      @Transactional public void delete(UserId id)
      Description copied from interface: UserRepository
      Hard-deletes the user identified by id. The FK cascade chain in V001 is responsible for removing every owned agent, conversation, and message (REQ-USR-006); the integration test in US-05-008 verifies this through the REST surface. A non-existent id is a silent no-op at this layer — the use case (US-05-008) is responsible for the 404 by reading the row first.
      Specified by:
      delete in interface UserRepository
